strengths: The dish is presented on a clean plate or surface with minimal distracting clutter.
The framing keeps the food as the clear subject of the photo.
The lighting is even enough to show the food's natural colors.
issues: Overhead or harsh lighting can flatten food and make it look less appetizing.
A busy or messy background competes with the dish for the viewer's attention.
Shooting straight down or straight on can hide a dish's height and texture.

suggestions.title: Shoot near a window in natural light
suggestions.reason: Soft, natural light renders food colors more accurately and avoids the harsh shadows that overhead artificial lighting tends to create.

suggestions.title: Clear the background
suggestions.reason: Removing unrelated objects (menus, condiment bottles, staff or other diners in frame) keeps the viewer's attention on the dish itself.

suggestions.title: Shoot from a 45-degree angle for dishes with height
suggestions.reason: An angled shot shows layers and texture better than a flat overhead or straight-on shot for most plated dishes.

suggestions.title: Add one small pop of color
suggestions.reason: A garnish, napkin, or sauce drizzle draws the eye and increases visual interest without changing the dish itself.
